references.text: Phinehas, son of Eleazar, is mentioned here as the one who showed zeal for God and stopped the plague in Israel, and he was given an everlasting priesthood.
Phinehas, son of Eleazar, was sent out to war against the Midianites with the holy articles and the trumpets.
Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, was sent as a messenger to the tribes on the east side of the Jordan.
Eleazar, son of Aaron, died and was buried in Gibeah, which belonged to his son Phinehas.
Phinehas, son of Eleazar, is mentioned in the genealogy as the overseer of the Levites.
Eleazar is mentioned in the lineage from Aaron through the sons of Levi.
Phinehas, son of Eleazar, was formerly leader over the keepers, and the Lord was with him.
The descendants of Phinehas are mentioned among those who returned from Babylon.
Exodus introduces the lineage, while Numbers 25:11 explains its theological basis through Phinehas' action.
Complementary description of Eleazar as head: genealogical basis (Exodus) versus functional responsibility (Numbers).
Exodus introduces the person; Numbers 25:7 shows his defining act that confirms the lineage's calling.
